en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands during low tide.
Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the country, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, spanning roughly 14,649 square kilometers.
The famous Chocolate Hills formation in Bohol consists of at least 1,268 symmetrical, cone-shaped limestone hills.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features a navigable underground river that flows for 8.2 kilometers directly into the sea.
Mount Mayon is highly active and has recorded over 50 historical eruptions since the year 1616.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, which plunges to 10,540 meters, making it the deepest point in the country.
The critically endangered Tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, has a remaining wild population of fewer than 600 individuals.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects a pristine coral reef spanning 97,030 hectares.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the country.
